prompt:
Create exactly ONE original PNG sprite sheet for a tiny ash-gray moth flight cycle. Genuine transparent RGBA background. Strict 2 columns by 2 rows grid, FOUR SINGLE-MOTH POSES TOTAL, precisely one whole moth in each cell. Square sheet, equal cells, very wide completely alpha-zero empty gutters and outer margins. No chart, labels or cell borders. No image references. Original ASHVEIL game art, no copying another game's pixels.

ART: unmistakable coarse hand-placed PIXEL ART, large clean angular pixel clusters, crisp stepped dark-charcoal outlines, small restrained palette of charcoal, ash gray, muted warm gray and bone-silver. Absolutely NO airbrush, soft shading, photorealistic fur or powder, noise halo, blur, atmospheric wash, glow, smoke, fog, dust, sparkles, motion streaks, shadows, ground, scenery, light source, checkerboard pattern, text or numbers. Empty areas including between antennae and between wing edges must be truly transparent, not black or gray paint.

MODEL LOCK: the SAME small ash moth in every cell, rigidly identical short fuzzy CHARCOAL HEAD, compact THORAX, tapered segmented ABDOMEN and exactly TWO ANTENNAE. One anatomically normal left forewing+hindwing and right forewing+hindwing; joined wing lobes read as one paired wing silhouette per side, never extra wings. Broad ash-gray wings have one simple broken charcoal cross-band and a sparse bone-colored scalloped edge, consistent in every pose. No human face, no eyespot faces, no humanoid limbs, no butterfly portrait. The head ALWAYS points straight to the TOP of the image. Dorsal view directly looking down on the BACK, with no change of camera angle or heading, no rotation, no side views. The body's exact source-pixel size, straight vertical centerline, thorax position and head-to-tail length stay identical in all four cells; only wings articulate at the fixed thorax attachment. Both antennae stay the same length and position. No bobbing or body translation.

PLACEMENT: local thorax anchor is exactly at the center of EACH equal cell. Even the widest fully spread moth including antennae fits inside the central 50 percent of its cell's width and height, NEVER more than 60 percent. Put a very generous fully transparent gap around every moth, including at the sheet edges. No body or wing crosses a cell boundary. Equal perceived body size in all cells, not four different moth species or four scale variants.

FOUR DISTINCT PHASES, ordered row-major, with unmistakably different wing silhouettes while the body/antennae remain fixed:
TOP LEFT: UPWARD RECOVERY — both wings raised steeply above the back in a narrow high-V. In the fixed dorsal projection the wings are strongly foreshortened to narrow angular slivers beside the thorax, with outer tips reaching slightly forward toward the head. This is an open raised-wing recovery, not the closed resting pose.
TOP RIGHT: FULLY SPREAD — both pairs fully extended horizontally to the left and right at the body plane, the broadest possible clear symmetrical moth silhouette, forewings broad and the smaller hindwing lobes behind them. Head stays straight up and the thorax exactly centered.
BOTTOM LEFT: DOWNWARD POWER STROKE — wings sweep below the body plane and backward toward the tail, drawn in the SAME fixed dorsal view as a distinctly broad backward/downward V, narrower than the fully spread pose but much wider than the recovery slivers. Forewing tips appear rearward of the thorax; body is not tilted or moved. Do not substitute the fully spread silhouette again.
BOTTOM RIGHT: FOLDED RECOVERY — wings fold very close along either side of the abdomen into a compact pointed tent-like silhouette, darkest narrowest pose, with consistent gray/bone wing markings partly hidden. This is closed near-body recovery and clearly different from the high-V top-left pose. The head, antennae, thorax and tail remain the same exact vertical model.

Only these four isolated insects on true transparency. Do not draw a swarm, extra flying insects, an attack, blood, debris or a background. Make the four different wing poses immediately legible and retain a stable body attachment anchor suitable for runtime instancing as tiny moths. Do not illustrate the whole colony or a scene.
